Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
4 October 2026 .
Brent $ 102.25 -0.11 % · Transits 1 (2026-09-27) · AI-assisted
01 Al Jazeera and jpost.com report Iran will keep the Strait of Hormuz shut until the US meets conditions set under the Islamabad pact, with Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf named as the source.

02 IMF PortWatch recorded 1 vessel transiting on 2026-09-27, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day; Investing.com reports Iraq's state tanker firm moved crude through the strait amid disruptions.

03 Brent crude stood at $102.25 as of 11:48 UTC, down 0.11% in the last session before the close; futures are shut.

Situation
The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic, with Tehran holding firm on its conditions for reopening. Al Jazeera reports Iran's closure stands until the US meets conditions set under the Islamabad pact, with Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf cited as the source of the declaration. A separate India Today report relaying a Tehran statement says reopening the strait has been Iran's stated objective while the US has kept nuclear talks at the center of its agenda. Brent crude stood at $102.25 as of 11:48 UTC, a change of -0.11% in the last session before the close; futures are shut. Fifty-six events were indexed in the past 24 hours, reflecting the pace of developments across the strait corridor. As of 11:50 UTC, 156 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, flat over 24 hours, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the elevated band, flat over 24 hours, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
